title: Max AI
summary: A Python framework for agents that take action.
text: Max AI A Python framework for agents that take action. Compose an agent from a model, instructions, and typed tools. Max AI connects the reasoning loop, execution environment, and context your application needs through explicit Python interfaces. v0.1.0 Python ≥ 3.11 Pydantic-based Async runtime Start with a working example. Define a tool, connect a model, and run your first task in the quickstart . Then explore the Agent API as your application grows.

summary: Choose a starting point for your application.
text: Build with Max AI # Choose a starting point for your application. ↗ Give your agent tools Turn Python functions into actions with validated inputs. ↗ Connect an MCP server Bring external tools into the same agent run. ↗ Get structured results Describe your output with a Pydantic model. ↗ Choose an environment Configure workspace files and tool execution.

title: Installation
summary: Max AI requires Python 3.11 or later . From a local checkout of this repository, install the project and its dependencies.
text: Installation # Max AI requires Python 3.11 or later . From a local checkout of this repository, install the project and its dependencies. uv pip Terminal Copy uv sync Terminal Copy python -m pip install -e . Using Ollama? Start the local server and download a model before running the examples: ollama pull qwen3:8b .

title: Your first agent
summary: An agent combines a model client with instructions and the tools it can call. These examples use a local Ollama model.
text: Your first agent # An agent combines a model client with instructions and the tools it can call. These examples use a local Ollama model. Agent with tools Structured output Define a typed function, register it with toolset , and let the agent use it to answer a question. agent.py Copy import asyncio from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.clients.ollama import OllamaChatCompletionClient from max_ai.capabilities.tools.decorator import tool from max_ai.core.model.llm import ModelConfig @tool def multiply (left: int , right: int ) -> int : """Multiply two integers.""" return left * right async def main (): # 1. Select a model client and declare its tool-calling support. client = OllamaChatCompletionClient( model= " qwen3:8b " , config=ModelConfig(supports_function_calling= True ), ) # 2. Compose the agent from its identity, client, and local toolset. agent = Agent( name= " math-assistant " , description= " Answers simple questions with a calculator tool. " , instructions= " Use the multiply tool when multiplication is needed. " , client=client, toolset=[multiply], ) # 3. Run a task and read the final assistant text. async with agent: result = await agent.run( " What is 19 multiplied by 23? " ) print (result.final_text) asyncio.run(main()) The @tool decorator builds the input schema from your function. The agent handles registration and dispatch. Explore function tools → Pass a Pydantic model as output_format to describe the result your application needs. structured_output.py Copy import asyncio from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.clients.ollama import OllamaChatCompletionClient from max_ai.core.model.llm import ModelConfig class Summary (BaseModel): title: str key_points: list [ str ] confidence: float = Field(ge= 0 , le= 1 ) async def main (): client = OllamaChatCompletionClient( model= " qwen3:8b " , config=ModelConfig(supports_function_calling= True ), ) agent = Agent( name= " summarizer " , description= " Summarizes reports as structured data. " , instructions= " Return a concise, faithful summary. " , client=client, output_format=Summary, ) async with agent: response = await agent.run( " Summarize the supplied report. " ) message = response.final_message if message and message.structured_output: print (message.structured_output.title) asyncio.run(main()) Read the validated result from the final message. Explore structured output → What happens during a run? Build the context The agent assembles instructions, tools, and enabled context providers. Call the model and execute tools The reasoning loop requests a response and dispatches tool calls. Read the result Use final_text or the structured output from the final message. The async context manager closes managed resources.

title: Agents
summary: Define an agent's identity, model client, tools, and execution policy. Then run a task or resume an existing run.
text: Agents Define an agent's identity, model client, tools, and execution policy. Then run a task or resume an existing run.

title: Agent configuration
summary: Agent needs an identity and a model client. The remaining arguments plug in tools, MCP connections, execution, context sources, or run policies. Defaults are selected for reasoning, workspace, and execution.
text: Agent configuration # Agent needs an identity and a model client. The remaining arguments plug in tools, MCP connections, execution, context sources, or run policies. Defaults are selected for reasoning, workspace, and execution. Agent constructor · max_ai.agents.Agent Copy def __init__ ( self, name: str , description: str , instructions: str , client: CoreChatCompletionClient, toolset: Sequence[CoreTool | Callable[..., Any]] | None = None , *, # Optional configuration follows the required arguments. mcp: Sequence[MCPServerConfig] | None = None , mcp_servers: Sequence[MCPServerConfig] | None = None , executor: ExecutorBase | None = None , workspace: WorkspaceBase | None = None , skills: CoreSkillRegistry | None = None , memory: CoreMemoryRegistry | None = None , knowledge: Sequence[CoreKnowledgeRegistry] | None = None , reasoning: BaseReasoning | None = None , max_iterations: int = 20 , idle_timeout: float = 300 , output_format: type[BaseModel] | None = None , completion_handlers: Sequence[CompletionHandler] | None = None , ) -> None : ... Required Identity All str : agent identity and behavioral instructions. Required Model CoreChatCompletionClient : for example, the Ollama, OpenAI, or OpenRouter client. Tools toolset Sequence[CoreTool | Callable] , optional; separate from MCP. Connections mcp Sequence[MCPServerConfig] , optional. Use mcp or mcp_servers , never both. Runtime Executor + workspace Optional ExecutorBase and WorkspaceBase ; defaults are LocalExecutor and LocalWorkspace . Context Skills, memory, knowledge Optional CoreSkillRegistry , CoreMemoryRegistry , and a sequence of CoreKnowledgeRegistry objects. Control Reasoning + limits Optional BaseReasoning ; max_iterations: int , idle_timeout: float , output_format: type[BaseModel] , and completion handlers. A run accepts task as text, one CoreMessage , a list of messages, or None ; it can also receive a RunContext and CancellationToken . Call await agent.run(task, run_context=...) for a result. Use run_stream() for text chunks, run_stream_events() for structured events, and resume(run_context) after an approval or user-input pause. AgentResponse contains final_text , finish_reason , usage, and the run context.

title: Run lifecycle
summary: run() returns a final AgentResponse ; run_stream() yields text chunks; run_stream_events() yields runtime events and the final response. A pause for approval or input preserves the run context so the caller can
text: Run lifecycle # Task + RunContext → PromptCtx → Reasoning loop → AgentResponse run() returns a final AgentResponse ; run_stream() yields text chunks; run_stream_events() yields runtime events and the final response. A pause for approval or input preserves the run context so the caller can resolve it and resume. The agent owns its executor sessions. Use it as an async context manager so close() runs when the scope exits.

title: Prompt layers
summary: Prompt layers turn agent configuration and optional registry data into model instructions. They are rendered for each run, then adapted to the selected provider's message format.
text: Prompt layers Prompt layers turn agent configuration and optional registry data into model instructions. They are rendered for each run, then adapted to the selected provider's message format.

title: From values to prompt
summary: The user task and tool schemas remain separate inputs. The diagram follows only the prompt instructions from configuration to the provider request.
text: From values to prompt # The user task and tool schemas remain separate inputs. The diagram follows only the prompt instructions from configuration to the provider request. 01 · Collect Agent + registries Read identity fields and collect configured skills, knowledge tool names, and memory context. Agent._prompt_variables() → 02 · Render Ordered templates Each active CoreLayer receives the shared values and renders its own Jinja2 template. layer.render(variables) → 03 · Package PromptCtx Rendered text is stored by layer class in rendered_layers , with the source stack and values. Agent._prompts() → 04 · Inject Model client The reasoning loop passes PromptCtx to client.run() ; the client builds provider-native messages. client.format_messages()

title: The prompt stack
summary: max_ai.agents.Agent._build_prompt_stack() creates these layers in this order. The first three are always present. Capability layers appear when the matching registry is passed to the agent.
text: The prompt stack # max_ai.agents.Agent._build_prompt_stack() creates these layers in this order. The first three are always present. Capability layers appear when the matching registry is passed to the agent. 01 AgentPolicyLayer Agent identity, description, developer instructions, and behavior policy. Always · agent fields 02 TaskAnalysisLayer Static guidance for interpreting the task, checking missing information, and deciding whether to plan or clarify. Always · static template 03 RenderingLayer Static response-format guidance for readable text, code, lists, links, and diagrams. Always · static template 04 SkillsLayer Renders available skill names and summaries after the skill registry is prepared. Full instructions stay in the materialized skill package. When skills is set 05 KnowledgeLayer Lets the model know which retrieval tools exist. Search results arrive later as tool-result messages. When knowledge is set 06 MemoryLayer Adds the current memory snapshot and describes available memory operations. When memory is set

title: Variable sources
summary: The agent collects values before rendering. A layer only reads the names used by its own template; it does not query a registry directly.
text: Variable sources # The agent collects values before rendering. A layer only reads the names used by its own template; it does not query a registry directly. Template Variables Source AgentPolicyLayer name , description , instructions Agent constructor SkillsLayer loaded_skills skills.get_skills() during prepare KnowledgeLayer retrieval_tools Tool names from knowledge registries MemoryLayer persistent_memories , memory_tools Scoped memory registry TaskAnalysisLayer — Static template text; no run variables RenderingLayer — Static template text; no run variables Not part of the prompt layers The user task and chat history are CoreMessage entries in RunContext . Tool schemas are sent as the separate tools argument to the model client. Knowledge results are added as tool-result messages after retrieval.

title: Rendering a variable
summary: The template declares where a value belongs. At run time CoreLayer.render() inserts values into that position and returns a string. For example, AgentPolicyLayer has this structure:
text: Rendering a variable # The template declares where a value belongs. At run time CoreLayer.render() inserts values into that position and returns a string. For example, AgentPolicyLayer has this structure: Jinja2 template Copy <identity> <name>{{ name }}</name> <description>{{ description }}</description> <instructions>{{ instructions }}</instructions> </identity> Agent values render into the placeholders ↓ Rendered layer text Copy <identity> <name>math-assistant</name> <description>Answers questions with a calculator.</description> <instructions>Use the multiply tool when needed.</instructions> </identity> Templates use Jinja2. `CoreLayer` validates required and optional placeholders when it is constructed; strict rendering surfaces missing values instead of silently producing incomplete instructions.

title: Model client injection
summary: The agent packages the ordered stack and its rendered strings in PromptCtx . The reasoning loop passes it into the client on every model call. The provider adapter decides how to form the actual request.
text: Model client injection # The agent packages the ordered stack and its rendered strings in PromptCtx . The reasoning loop passes it into the client on every model call. The provider adapter decides how to form the actual request. Agent._prompts() and BaseReasoning._call_llm() Copy variables = await self._prompt_variables(ctx) prompts = PromptCtx( stack=self._stack, variables=variables, rendered_layers={ type(layer): layer.render(variables) for layer in self._stack }, ) # ReactLoop supplies prompt context and tool schemas separately. result = await self.client.run( ctx=self._model_context(ctx, transient_messages), prompts=prompts, tools=tools, ) For Ollama, non-empty rendered layers are joined with blank lines into a system message. Conversation history and the current task follow as messages. Other model clients can assemble those pieces differently to match their provider APIs.

title: Create a custom layer
summary: A CoreLayer subclass defines a template, its required variables, and optional variables. The framework's generic LayerContainer can hold layers and replace defaults.
text: Create a custom layer # A CoreLayer subclass defines a template, its required variables, and optional variables. The framework's generic LayerContainer can hold layers and replace defaults. Layer authoring · generic stack API Copy from max_ai.capabilities.stacks.agent_policy_layer import AgentPolicyLayer from max_ai.core.stacks.container import LayerContainer from max_ai.types.stacks import PromptCtx policy = AgentPolicyLayer( template=( '<name>{{ name }}</name>\n' '<description>{{ description }}</description>\n' '<instructions>{{ instructions }}</instructions>' ), ) variables = { 'name': 'support', 'description': 'A support assistant', 'instructions': 'Answer with concise, grounded help.', } stack = LayerContainer([policy]) prompt = PromptCtx( stack=stack, variables=variables, rendered_layers={type(layer): layer.render(variables) for layer in stack}, ) Important: this demonstrates the generic layer and PromptCtx APIs. The current public max_ai.agents.Agent builds its stack inside _build_prompt_stack() ; it does not yet accept prompt_layers= in its constructor. So a custom stack is not currently injectable into that Agent without extending the runtime.

title: Tools & dispatch
summary: Give your agent actions with typed Python functions or a custom CoreTool. The registry and dispatcher connect model requests to your implementation.
text: Tools & dispatch Give your agent actions with typed Python functions or a custom CoreTool. The registry and dispatcher connect model requests to your implementation.

title: Registry and dispatch
summary: Tools declare callable schemas. ToolRegistry indexes them, and ToolDispatcher validates parameters, applies approval rules, and routes each call either to a host adapter or through EnvironmentManager to the con
text: Registry and dispatch # Tools declare callable schemas. ToolRegistry indexes them, and ToolDispatcher validates parameters, applies approval rules, and routes each call either to a host adapter or through EnvironmentManager to the configured executor. tools.py Copy from max_ai.capabilities.tools.decorator import tool @tool def calculate_total (price: float , quantity: int ) -> float : """Calculate the total price for a quantity of items.""" return price * quantity

title: Functions as tools
summary: Decorate a function with @tool and pass the resulting object in the agent's toolset . Max AI builds the JSON schema from type hints, uses the docstring as its description, validates arguments, and invokes the f
text: Functions as tools # Decorate a function with @tool and pass the resulting object in the agent's toolset . Max AI builds the JSON schema from type hints, uses the docstring as its description, validates arguments, and invokes the function. Regular and async functions are supported. tools.py Copy from max_ai.capabilities.tools.decorator import tool @tool def calculate_total (price: float , quantity: int ) -> float : """Calculate the total price for a quantity of items.""" return price * quantity @tool (approval_mode= " ask_for_approval " ) async def reserve_item (sku: str , quantity: int ) -> dict : """Reserve stock for an item.""" return await inventory.reserve(sku, quantity) In the async example, inventory is your application's inventory service. The registration snippet assumes an imported Agent , a configured client , and an async function. Decorated functions use auto_approval by default. Use approval_mode="ask_for_approval" when an action should wait for a person. Set a custom name or description with @tool(name="…", description="…") . Type the first parameter as ToolContext if the function needs run-specific dependencies. agent.py · register and run Copy agent = Agent( name= " shop-assistant " , description= " Answers shopping questions. " , instructions= " Use calculate_total for purchase totals. " , client=client, toolset=[calculate_total, reserve_item], ) async with agent: result = await agent.run( " What is 3 items at $12.50 each? " ) print (result.final_text)

title: Native tools with CoreTool
summary: Subclass CoreTool when you need direct control over the input schema and execution. Implement the parameters property and async execute() method. The dispatcher validates the call first; your implementation ret
text: Native tools with CoreTool # Subclass CoreTool when you need direct control over the input schema and execution. Implement the parameters property and async execute() method. The dispatcher validates the call first; your implementation returns a ToolResult tied to the call ID. tax_tool.py Copy from typing import Any from max_ai.base import CoreTool from max_ai.base.tools import ToolContext from max_ai.core.termination import CancellationToken from max_ai.types.tool_call import ToolCallRecord, ToolResult from max_ai.types.tools import ToolApprovalMode class AddTaxTool (CoreTool): def __init__ ( self ) -> None : super (). __init__ ( name= " add_tax " , description= " Add a tax rate to an amount. " , approval_mode=ToolApprovalMode.AUTO_APPROVED, ) @property def parameters ( self ) -> dict [ str , Any]: return { " type " : " object " , " properties " : { " amount " : { " type " : " number " , " description " : " Pre-tax amount. " }, " rate " : { " type " : " number " , " description " : " Rate, e.g. 0.08 for 8 % . " }, }, " required " : [ " amount " , " rate " ], " additionalProperties " : False , } async def execute ( self , tool_request: ToolCallRecord, tool_context: ToolContext | None = None , cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None , ) -> ToolResult: amount = float (tool_request.parameters[ " amount " ]) rate = float (tool_request.parameters[ " rate " ]) total = round (amount * ( 1 + rate), 2 ) return ToolResult.success_result(tool_request.id, { " total " : total}) Pass an instance to the agent with toolset=[AddTaxTool()] . Define inputs with JSON Schema and choose the approval mode in super().__init__() . Read application dependencies from tool_context.deps , and return ToolResult.tool_failure(tool_request.id, "reason") on failure. A regular CoreTool runs in the agent process; use CoreRuntimeTool when implementation must run through the configured isolated runtime.

title: The reasoning loop
summary: BaseReasoning is the extension contract; ReactLoop is the default implementation. It coordinates model calls, tool dispatch, streamed events, iteration limits, cancellation, and pause/resume state.
text: The reasoning loop # BaseReasoning is the extension contract; ReactLoop is the default implementation. It coordinates model calls, tool dispatch, streamed events, iteration limits, cancellation, and pause/resume state. RunContext → Model client → Tool dispatcher → Events + state ↺

title: Runtime services
text: Runtime services # 05 Environment manager Manages execution sessions around workspace and executor. 06 Event bus Emits model, tool, approval, input, and completion events. 07 Completion gate Evaluates whether a run may report a completed outcome. 08 Run context Holds messages, tool state, plan, completion evidence, and resumable state. 09 Persistence Stores serialized run context for checkpoints and continuation. 10 Middleware & telemetry Logging, tracing, and observability hooks around runtime work. 11 Messages & events Typed conversation messages and runtime event contracts. 12 Provider clients Ollama, OpenAI, and OpenRouter implement the model client contract.

title: Capabilities
summary: Workspaces, execution providers, and context registries supply capabilities around the core Agent. Configure only the providers this application needs.
text: Capabilities Workspaces, execution providers, and context registries supply capabilities around the core Agent. Configure only the providers this application needs.

title: Workspace and execution
summary: WorkspaceBase owns persistent user files and skill materialization. ExecutorBase runs executor-routed tools. EnvironmentManager manages sessions linking the two. Available executors are Local, Docker, and Modal
text: Workspace and execution # WorkspaceBase owns persistent user files and skill materialization. ExecutorBase runs executor-routed tools. EnvironmentManager manages sessions linking the two. Available executors are Local, Docker, and Modal; local execution runs on the host and is not a sandbox. WorkspaceBase EnvironmentManager ExecutorBase

title: Memory, skills, and knowledge
summary: Memory is scoped to a user and session. Skills provide instructions and resources. Knowledge registries expose retrieval tools. Context registries are also available as independent providers for context data. E
text: Memory, skills, and knowledge # Memory is scoped to a user and session. Skills provide instructions and resources. Knowledge registries expose retrieval tools. Context registries are also available as independent providers for context data. Each capability has provider implementations under max_ai.capabilities , with config models kept in _model.py .

title: Integrations
summary: Connect external tools, return structured data, and handle approvals using the same agent runtime.
text: Integrations Connect external tools, return structured data, and handle approvals using the same agent runtime.

title: Connect MCP servers
summary: Keep remote capabilities in the mcp or mcp_servers list, separate from local Python toolset . The agent connects servers for a run, discovers tools, dispatches calls, and closes its MCP sessions afterward. Both
text: Connect MCP servers # Keep remote capabilities in the mcp or mcp_servers list, separate from local Python toolset . The agent connects servers for a run, discovers tools, dispatches calls, and closes its MCP sessions afterward. Both server configs and the mixed server list are Pydantic models with JSON round-trip helpers. mcp_config.py Copy import os from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.clients.ollama import OllamaChatCompletionClient from max_ai.capabilities.mcp import ( HTTPServerConfig, StdioMCPServerConfig, serialize_mcp_servers, deserialize_mcp_servers, ) servers = [ StdioMCPServerConfig( server_id= "local-docs" , command= "your-mcp-server" , ), HTTPServerConfig( server_id= "tickets" , url= "https://your-mcp.example/mcp" , token=os.environ[ "TICKETS_MCP_TOKEN" ], ), ] stored_json = serialize_mcp_servers(servers) restored_servers = deserialize_mcp_servers(stored_json) agent = Agent( name= "support" , description= "A support assistant" , instructions= "Use connected tools when useful." , client=OllamaChatCompletionClient(model= "qwen3:8b" ), mcp_servers=restored_servers, ) Replace the example server command and URL with real MCP endpoints. Keep tokens and sensitive headers in a secret store when persisting serialized configs. MCP SDK support is declared in the repository's pyproject.toml .

title: Structured output
summary: Pass a Pydantic model class as output_format . The final assistant message carries the validated model instance, so application code can use typed fields directly.
text: Structured output # Pass a Pydantic model class as output_format . The final assistant message carries the validated model instance, so application code can use typed fields directly. structured_output.py Copy import asyncio from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from max_ai.agents import Agent from max_ai.capabilities.clients.ollama import OllamaChatCompletionClient from max_ai.core.model.llm import ModelConfig class Summary (BaseModel): title: str key_points: list [ str ] confidence: float = Field(ge= 0 , le= 1 ) async def main (): client = OllamaChatCompletionClient( model= "qwen3:8b" , config=ModelConfig(supports_function_calling= True ), ) agent = Agent( name= "summarizer" , description= "Summarizes reports as structured data." , instructions= "Return a concise, faithful summary." , client=client, output_format=Summary, ) async with agent: response = await agent.run( "Summarize the supplied report." ) message = response.final_message if message and message.structured_output: print (message.structured_output.title) asyncio.run(main()) The field constraints come from Pydantic. Use a model/provider combination that supports structured output for best results.

title: Approvals and resume
summary: Set a tool's approval mode to ask_for_approval . The run returns with pending approval records. A trusted reviewer can approve or reject the call, then the application resumes the same RunContext .
text: Approvals and resume # Set a tool's approval mode to ask_for_approval . The run returns with pending approval records. A trusted reviewer can approve or reject the call, then the application resumes the same RunContext . approval_flow.py · inside an async application Copy from max_ai.capabilities.tools.decorator import tool @tool (approval_mode= "ask_for_approval" ) def publish_report (report_id: str ) -> str : """Publish a report through the application's publishing service.""" return publisher.publish(report_id) agent = Agent( name= "publisher" , description= "Publishes reports after review." , instructions= "Use publish_report when asked to publish." , client=client, # configured model client toolset=[publish_report], ) response = await agent.run( "Publish report R-42" ) if response.needs_approval: # Wait for your UI or service to obtain a reviewer decision. call = response.pending_approvals[ 0 ] call.approve(reason= "Approved by the assigned reviewer" ) response = await agent.resume(run_context=response.context) This is the approval decision point in application code; connect the call to your actual review workflow. The agent returns AgentResponse with pending approvals and resumable run context.
